_about: Generated by scripts/build-catalogs.py; do not edit. Edit docs/skill-keywords.json (FHSkillz) or external/index.json (external library).

items.name: jail-approval-gate
items.use_for: Classify every intended action into approval tiers BEFORE acting — never / per-action approval / batchable approval / auto-allowed — and fail closed: irreversible, external, durable, spend, or sensitive-data actions pause for a human with a proper approval request (what, why, blast radius, reversibility, safer alternative). Use at the start of any agentic run that will act on the world (send, publish, deploy, delete, buy, write durable memory, contact someone), when the user asks "what will you do without asking me", or when another skill's plan contains approval_required items.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for pure analysis/drafting tasks that touch nothing external.
use_cases: Pause before AI sends, buys or deletes
Sort planned actions by risk

items.name: jail-bmc
items.use_for: Build or evaluate a nine-block Business Model Canvas (customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships, cost structure) using evidence — every material element marked validated vs hypothesis, with the riskiest assumptions and the experiments to test them. Use when asked for a "business model canvas", "BMC", "map the business model", evaluating a venture/product idea's model, or pressure-testing how a business makes money.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for macro scans or competitive self-assessment (jail-strategy), or entity/legal-structure questions.
use_cases: Map how a business makes money
Pressure-test a new venture
Find the riskiest assumptions

items.name: jail-council
items.use_for: Convene an LLM COUNCIL for maximum-accuracy answers to consequential or contested questions: 3–5 independent models answer blind, adversarially review each other's ANONYMIZED answers, disputed facts get a targeted verification round, and a chairman synthesizes by evidence — never by vote — preserving dissent. Two lanes: FULL protocol for maximum stakes, and a MINI-COUNCIL (3 blind answers + one anonymized review round) for everyday contested calls. Cost is disclosed, never a gate. Use when the user says "convene the council", "ask multiple models", "get a second/third opinion", "maximum accuracy", "I need this answer to be right", "quick council" / "mini council" / "council-check this", or when jail-verify / jail-decide / jail-rate / jail-prompt escalate a high-stakes contested call.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for parallel division of labor across different subtasks (jail-orchestrate) or for questions with no knowable answer (STOP those).
use_cases: Get several AI models to cross-check an answer
High-stakes contested question

items.name: jail-cpr
items.use_for: Build a CPR (Context, Purpose, Results) as a DOCX/PDF. DESIGN: build or design an agenda, prep a meeting. COMMIT: personal or team commitment contract for a quarter or "tour", no meeting. DEBRIEF: pull decisions, action items, "what did we decide" and "who owes what" from a transcript; score a period.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for generic task/owner scoping (jail-task-contract) or turning a decision into a process (jail-plan).
use_cases: Build a meeting agenda
Pull decisions and owners from a transcript
Quarterly commitment plan

items.name: jail-decide
items.use_for: Turn a choice into a defensible DECISION PACKAGE: options incl. do-nothing, criteria first, one recommendation with confidence and change-conditions. Use for "which should we pick", "should we do X or Y", "build vs buy", "is this worth doing", "help me decide", "run the numbers on A vs B and pick one", "cheaper over N years".
items.not_for: Do NOT use to score one subject 0-10 (jail-rate), gather evidence (jail-research), or attack an option (jail-red-team).
use_cases: Pick between two or more options
Build vs buy call
Defend a choice to an owner or board

items.name: jail-diagnose
items.use_for: Feedback-loop-first diagnosis of hard defects — bugs, performance regressions, failing workflows, broken pipelines, "it sometimes doesn't work": build a tight red-capable reproduction signal BEFORE any hypothesizing, then minimize → hypothesize → instrument → fix → prove with a mandatory regression case. Use when the user says "debug this", "diagnose", reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow/flaky, or when a fix attempt failed and the cause is unclear.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to verify a finished deliverable (jail-verify) or to iterate a working thing toward a better metric (jail-lab).
use_cases: Find why something keeps breaking
Prove a fix with a regression check

items.name: jail-handoff
items.use_for: Compact the current session into a BATON — a handoff document a fresh agent (or tomorrow's session, or a smaller-context model) can pick up and continue from without re-reading everything: state of work, decisions with why, live references to artifacts (never duplicated), next actions, and which skills to invoke. Use when context is filling up, a session is ending mid-work, the user says "hand this off", "save where we are", "continue this later/elsewhere", or work must move to another agent/model — and OFFER it proactively on context-pressure signals (long session, approaching compaction, recall degrading) instead of waiting to be asked.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for the in-run structured handoff between skills (the JAIL-HANDOFF block) or for storing durable lessons (jail-memory).
keywords: pick up where I left off
use_cases: Save where you are before a chat ends
Hand work to another agent or model

items.name: jail-lab
items.use_for: Run a metric-driven EXPERIMENT LOOP on anything improvable — a prompt, a skill, code, content, a workflow, a landing page: declare one metric and a budget, then propose → bounded run → measure → keep/discard → log every experiment in an append-only audit ledger with cited evidence. Use when the user wants to "iterate until it's better", "optimize this", "run experiments", "A/B this", "tune it", improve something measurable, or turn a vague "make it better" into disciplined trials.
items.not_for: Do NOT use when no measurable metric can exist (taste-only judgments — use jail-rate for a scored assessment) or for one-shot verification (jail-verify).
use_cases: Improve something measurable with small experiments
A/B test a page or prompt

items.name: jail-memory
items.use_for: Govern project decision logs, verdict ledgers and lessons: what enters, stays in, and leaves durable project knowledge — provenance-checked, deduplicated, classified, superseded-not- deleted — and run the LEARNING POSTMORTEM ritual that turns finished work into stored lessons. Implemented as a MARKDOWN MEMORY SYSTEM: a MEMORY.md index plus one dated, provenance-headed .md file per entry, written to the project workspace so it travels, diffs in git, and works on any platform. Use when saving lessons/decisions/context for future sessions ("remember this", "save that for next time"), when retrieving prior context for a new task, after completed or failed projects ("what did we learn"), or when another skill proposes a durable write.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for in-conversation working notes, or for the adoption review of raw inbound data (jail-quarantine — that gate runs first).
use_cases: Log a project decision with its source
Run a lessons-learned postmortem

items.name: jail-orchestrate
items.use_for: Run long or parallel work as one coordinated system — decide when delegation earns its cost, assign non-overlapping scopes with minimum sufficient context, keep a dependency graph and resume ledger, audit progress against real tool results, reconcile conflicts by evidence, and integrate one final result. Includes a SOLO lane: the same ledger discipline for ONE agent on long multi-part work (no subagents needed). Use when work splits across parallel agents or research streams ("fan this out", "use subagents", "divide this up"), for long-horizon multi-part execution ("keep a resume ledger", "track this build so we can resume"), or when jail-research/jail-task-contract hands off a parallelizable plan.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for short single-sitting tasks or for defining the human-run process itself (jail-plan).
use_cases: Split a big job across AI helpers
Track a long build so it can resume

items.name: jail-plan
items.use_for: Turn intent into an executable plan — two lanes. OPERATE: convert a decision, recommendation, or idea into a runnable OPERATING WORKFLOW (trigger, inputs, actions, tool, owner, approval, output, evidence, metric, frequency, risk, testable completion). MAP: navigate work too big and foggy for one session by charting a MAP of DECISION TICKETS and resolving them one at a time until the path to a named destination is clear. Use when analysis stops at "you should…" and someone must actually run it ("make this operational", "turn this into a process", "who does what", "how do we actually do this"), OR when a loose, months-long idea arrives with no clear path ("we should overhaul X", "figure out how to enter Y", "no idea where to start").
items.not_for: Do NOT use to scope a single up-front task (jail-task-contract) or to coordinate a multi-agent run (jail-orchestrate).
use_cases: Turn a decision into a runnable process
Map a foggy multi-month goal
Owner, tool and metric for each step

items.name: jail-prompt
items.use_for: Turn a vague goal into an engineered, verifiable prompt, a multi-agent prompt set (orchestrator + subagent briefs), or a STOP when AI is the wrong tool. Use when the user has an outcome but no real prompt, says "make this prompt better", "write me a prompt", "is AI the right tool", or wants prompts for subagents.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to run a finished prompt, proofread, plain chat, do research (jail-research), or run a multi-agent job (jail-orchestrate).
use_cases: Turn a goal into a tested prompt
Decide if AI is the right tool
Write prompts for a team of AI agents
Write a prompt for ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok or Perplexity

items.name: jail-prospect
items.use_for: Screen a US private company from FREE, authoritative sources — two lanes: PROSPECT (business-brokering sell-side + consulting lens, scored brief with Likelihood-to-Sell and Consulting-Opportunity) and COMPANY SNAPSHOT (the same OSINT discipline pointed at vendor due-diligence, competitor reads, or partnership vetting). Never fabricates financials. Use when evaluating whether to approach an owner about selling or consulting, OR when vetting any named private company before relying on it. Triggers: "research this company", "is this a good brokerage prospect", "prospect brief", "should I approach this owner", "sell-side screen", "consulting opportunity", "snapshot this vendor/company", "vet this vendor", "due diligence on X", "are they solid enough to sign with", "competitor read on X".
use_cases: Screen a business before calling the owner
Likelihood-to-sell score
Vet a vendor or partner
Competitor snapshot

items.name: jail-prototype
items.use_for: Build a THROWAWAY prototype whose only job is to answer a stated design question — "does this logic/state model feel right?", "what should this look like?", "will this approach hold?" — then fold the validated answer into real work, register it in the SPIKE LEDGER (so answered questions are never re-prototyped), and discard the prototype. Use when the user wants to sanity-check a design, explore variations, "mock something up to see", "try it before we build it", or when jail-decide/jail-bmc needs a cheap experiment answered by building.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for production implementation, metric-driven iteration on an existing thing (jail-lab), or verification of finished work (jail-verify).
use_cases: Quick throwaway mock-up to answer a design question
Test a page layout before building

items.name: jail-py-toolkit
items.use_for: Runnable machine checks for FHSkillz (Python 3.8+, stdlib). Use when a skill asks for a machine check: secret or PII scans; prompt, chain and handoff lints; citation, quote, label and score-math checks; model trials; skill structure lint; rating validate/save/variance; jail-lab experiment ledgers (log, best-so-far, compare).
items.not_for: Do NOT use to write prompts (jail-prompt) or make ratings (jail-rate).
use_cases: Run code checks for secrets, prompts and citations
Validate a skill folder

items.name: jail-quarantine
items.use_for: Two-sided data discipline: (1) ADOPTION GATE — discovered, scraped, bulk- captured, or extracted data lands as quarantined draft and never flows into decisions, memory, or outputs until reviewed and adopted; (2) SENSITIVE HALT — on detecting protected data (credentials, keys, tokens, PII, PHI, CUI, client-confidential, regulated, IP), stop processing that item and fail closed rather than degrade to an unsafe path. Includes an INLINE SCAN lane for everyday small pastes ("quick check this before we use it"). Use when ingesting external/bulk content (scrapes, imports, brain-dumps, inboxes, transcripts, found files), when pasting third-party content into the conversation (vendor emails, forwarded threads, snippets), when handling anything that might contain secrets or regulated data, or when another skill flags sensitive inputs.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for the user's own directly-supplied working text they've asked you to edit.
use_cases: Check pasted or scraped data before using it
Stop on secrets or personal data

items.name: jail-questionnaire
items.use_for: Turn what you can't answer alone into a questionnaire someone else fills in: a client discovery intake before an engagement, or the open questions behind a decision, sent to an owner, CFO or expert. Most important first, one idea per question, an answer slot under each. Use for "intake form", "discovery questions", "what should I ask them".
items.not_for: Do NOT use to ask the user questions live (jail-task-contract) or for meeting agendas (jail-cpr).
use_cases: Client discovery intake
Questions for an owner or CFO
Fill gaps behind a stuck decision

items.name: jail-rate
items.use_for: Rate, score, grade, judge, or evaluate ANY named subject 0.0-10.0 (software, code, hardware, small business, idea, plan, program, content, a person's public work role) with a weighted rubric, cited evidence, ranked fixes, and current to projected scores. Triggers: "rate this", "give it a 0-10", "how would you grade", "is this idea any good".
items.not_for: Do NOT use for AI skill folders (jail-rate-skill), prospect calls (jail-prospect), SWOT (jail-strategy).
use_cases: Score a product, plan or business 0-10
Compare a vendor against a rubric
List fixes ranked by impact

items.name: jail-rate-skill
items.use_for: Evaluate and rate another AI skill (its SKILL.md and support files) using the standardized 10-category Skill Rating Matrix, IDE Compatibility Matrix, and CLI Compatibility Matrix. Triggers: "/jail-rate-skill", "rate this skill", "evaluate this skill", "score this skill".
use_cases: Grade an AI skill's build quality
Check which tools a skill works in

items.name: jail-red-team
items.use_for: Pressure-test a plan, recommendation, design, or belief before it ships: steelman it, then find hidden assumptions, missing stakeholders, dependency failures and second-order effects, each with a cheapest falsifier and a verdict. Use for "poke holes in this", "what am I missing", "devil's advocate", "pre-mortem this", irreversible calls.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to check a finished deliverable (jail-verify) or for trivial choices.
use_cases: Find weak spots in a plan
Pre-mortem before launch
Challenge a recommendation

items.name: jail-research
items.use_for: Research a question into two paired outputs: a cited synthesized answer plus an auditable evidence packet (tiered dated sources, contradictions, honest gaps). Use for "research X", "find evidence for", "what does the data say", "verify this claim", or when jail-decide, jail-strategy, or jail-rate need grounding.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for US private-company sell-side screens (jail-prospect) or when the user already has all facts (jail-summarize).
use_cases: Cited answer with an evidence packet
Check a claim before you repeat it
Ground a decision or rating in sources

items.name: jail-skill-miner
items.use_for: Mine a codebase, chat history, or document set for plugin-worthy SKILLS — reusable disciplines, not app features — then dedupe candidates against the installed plugin before authoring anything. Also the suite's SELF- MAINTENANCE loop: failed eval cases and corrections repeated across sessions auto-nominate skill fixes/deltas. Use when the user asks to "extract skills from", "mine this repo/history for skills", "what disciplines does this codebase enforce", "should this become a skill", when evaluating candidate-skill lists from other tools/models, or when an eval failure / repeated correction needs turning into a skill change.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to author an already-approved skill from scratch (follow repo conventions directly) or to rate an existing skill (jail-rate-skill).
use_cases: Spot repeated work that should become a skill
Dedupe skill ideas against the suite

items.name: jail-strategy
items.use_for: Run one evidence-grounded strategy analysis: SWOT then TOWS (INTERNAL), PESTLE with tripwires (MACRO), COMPETITIVE (Porter's five forces, competitor tiers, profile cards), or a FULL SWEEP. Use for "SWOT", "TOWS", "PESTLE", "macro trends", "external factors", "five forces", "competitor analysis", "competitive landscape", "full strategy picture".
items.not_for: Do NOT use for business models (jail-bmc), 0-10 scores (jail-rate), or bare research (jail-research).
use_cases: SWOT and TOWS for a client
PESTLE macro scan
Competitor analysis for a local market

items.name: jail-summarize
items.use_for: Turn analysis or technical findings into a decision-forcing brief for a board, CEO, owner, or client: lead with the answer, translate tech to business cost and risk, end on one recommendation. Use for "summarize this for the board/CEO/owner", "make this executive-ready", "translate this technical finding", decision memos.
items.not_for: Do NOT use for working notes, raw research (jail-research), full option analysis (jail-decide), meeting recaps (jail-cpr).
use_cases: Brief an owner or board
Turn a technical finding into business terms
One-page decision memo

items.name: jail-task-contract
items.use_for: Turn an ambiguous, multithreaded, or high-stakes request into a 14-field TASK CONTRACT with testable acceptance criteria before work starts, and guard scope after: a material change in goal, audience, data class, output, or authority is a NEW contract. Use for scoping a task or client engagement, "make sure we're aligned", drifting revisions.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to engineer a prompt (jail-prompt), run a process (jail-plan), or for trivial one-step asks.
use_cases: Agree scope before a big job
Write a testable finish line
Catch scope creep mid-project

items.name: jail-verify
items.use_for: Independently verify a finished output against its task contract, with artifacts from the current run, BEFORE it ships. Use when work claims done: "verify this", "check before we send", "is this actually complete", "agent says it's done, check", after multi-agent runs, or before consequential deliverables.
items.not_for: Do NOT use to score 0-10 (jail-rate), rate a skill directory (jail-rate-skill), or red-team a forming plan (jail-red-team).
use_cases: Check work before it ships
Prove an agent's 'done' claim
Pass/fail verdict with evidence

items.name: teach
items.use_for: Use it to learn a new skill or concept yourself, step by step, in a workspace of lessons and notes.
use_cases: Learn a new topic step by step
Build your own lesson notes

items.name: wait-what
items.use_for: Use it when an AI answer didn't make sense: it asks for a simpler re-explanation with more context.
use_cases: Ask AI to re-explain something simply

items.name: tdd
items.use_for: Use it on software projects to build features or fix bugs test-first (red, green, refactor).
use_cases: Build a feature test-first
Fix a bug with a failing test first

items.name: code-review
items.use_for: Use it on software projects to review code changes against the repo's standards and the original spec, side by side.
use_cases: Review a code change against the spec

items.name: to-tickets
items.use_for: Use it on software projects to split a plan into small tickets, each a thin working slice, with what blocks what.
use_cases: Split a plan into small tickets
Order work by what blocks what

items.name: wizard
items.use_for: Use it when setup steps only a person can do (dashboards, credentials) need a guided step-by-step script.
use_cases: Guided script for manual setup steps

items.name: writing-fragments / writing-beats / writing-shape
items.use_for: Use it to turn rough notes into an article: collect fragments, order them into beats, then shape paragraphs. Possible fit for the book project.
use_cases: Turn rough notes into an article
Outline a book chapter

items.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
items.use_for: Use it to block risky git commands (force push, hard reset) in Claude Code with hooks.
use_cases: Block risky git commands in Claude Code

items.name: ponytail
items.use_for: Use it while writing or fixing code to keep changes as small as possible. It makes the AI reuse what already exists, skip extras nobody asked for, and say what it left out.
use_cases: Keep code changes small
Stop AI adding unrequested extras

items.name: ponytail-review
items.use_for: Use it to check a code change or pull request before it ships. It finds bugs, security holes, missing tests and extra code, and explains each problem in plain English with a fix.
use_cases: Check a pull request before it ships

items.name: ponytail-audit
items.use_for: Use it when you take over a codebase, like a client's website or app. It reads the whole project and gives a ranked list of what is broken, risky or can be deleted, without changing anything.
use_cases: Audit a client's app or website you took over
Ranked list of what's broken or risky

items.name: creating-financial-models
items.use_for: Use it when you need to put a dollar value on a business, like a company you might help sell. It builds a discounted cash flow (DCF) model and shows how the value changes if growth or interest rates change. It talks about Monte Carlo too, but the scripts don't do that part.
use_cases: Value a business for a sale
Build a discounted cash flow model

items.name: analyzing-financial-statements
items.use_for: Use it when a client hands you their income statement and balance sheet. It works out the key ratios (profit margins, how much cash they have, how much debt) and says in plain words whether each looks healthy. It is built for public companies, so small-business owner add-backs need adding by hand.
use_cases: Work out a client's key financial ratios
Read an income statement and balance sheet

items.name: applying-brand-guidelines
items.use_for: Use it as a starting template when you want Claude to make every document match one client's colors, fonts and tone. The example brand is a made-up company, so you swap in the client's real brand first.
use_cases: Make every document match a client's brand
